threads.summary: The acceptance names one command for two properties, and that command can see only one of them. `git grep -n blocking -- packs` cannot `return one weighting sentence per craft`, because no weighting sentence contains the word `blocking`.
threads.evidence: At ca25ec76 `git grep -n blocking -- packs` exits 1 with no output. The five weighting sentences are `Weigh in this order — a shape finding never outranks a correctness finding.`, `Weigh in listed order.`, `Weigh in listed order: nothing below reproduction holds...`, `Weigh in listed order, except that the accessibility floor...` and `Weigh in listed order, and a claim with no source at all is read first.` -- none names a `blocking` value, which is exactly what the FIRST half of the same clause demands. The two halves are mutually exclusive under one grep. B1.1's Goal states it correctly in two commands (`git grep -n blocking -- packs then returns zero law and each craft's weighting sentence names no blocking value`); the whole-run acceptance compressed that into one and broke it.
threads.state_of_the_tree: Both properties hold. No craft names a blocking value; each of the five carries exactly one weighting sentence; the law is at rules/verification.md §10. tests/test_verification_model.py's BlockingLawOwnershipTest enforces both in the suite -- assertNotIn('blocking', craft) for all five packs, and a count of exactly one `outranks|listed order` per deliverable entry, with the entry's kind resolved through `adapter_spec(pack).artifact_kind` rather than a copied list.
threads.cause: An acceptance sentence written as prose about a command rather than as the command's expected output. It reads as satisfiable and is not, so a reader who runs it and gets nothing cannot tell a delivered run from an undelivered one.
threads.remedy: For the successor root: two commands, as B1.1's own Goal already had them -- `git grep -n blocking -- packs` returns nothing, and `git grep -c 'Weigh in' packs/*/references/craft.md` returns 1 for each of the five.
